column2: Retain seventy sons in Samaria and the letter to Samaria's rulers, elders and the sons' guardians. The city in the address is Samaria, not Jezreel; guardians represents the caretaking role without assigning an exact office.

Retain the letter's temporal opening, the recipients' possession of their master's sons, chariot force, horses, fortified cities and weapons. Cities is plural in the selected text; the inventory is not reduced to a single fortress.

Retain good and upright as the qualifications for selecting a son, enthronement on his father's throne and fighting for their master's house. The challenge is Jehu's speech, not an editorial instruction to choose a legitimate successor.
Retain great fear, Behold, the two kings' inability to stand and the recipients' question about their own resistance. The two kings are not given new names within the speech.

Retain the four groups' submission, refusal to make anyone king and future we will do what is good in your eyes. The final clause is not changed into an imperative do what seems good to you; the selected speakers undertake the action.

Retain the second letter, conditional loyalty and obedience, demand for heads, tomorrow's hour and Jezreel. Plural heads naturally renders the collective singular head of the men. Seventy royal sons and their upbringing by prominent city men remain distinct from the address.

Retain the letter's arrival, seizure and slaughter of seventy sons, heads in baskets and delivery to Jezreel. The lethal action and number are explicit; no additional method beyond the stated slaughter and heads is described.
Retain the messenger's report and order for two mounds at the gate doorway until morning. The location and interval remain, and no purpose for the display is added.

Retain morning, Jehu at the gateway, all the people, You are righteous, his admitted conspiracy and killing, and the question who struck these. The rhetorical self-positioning is not turned into the narrator's absolution of the crowd.

Retain See and unresolved Appho, the denial that any of the Lord's word falls to the ground, Ahab's house and fulfillment through Elijah. Appho's capitalization and dashes are inherited editorial choices, not proof of a proper name.
column3: Does affo function as an emphatic or temporal particle here, and should its treatment be coordinated with the distinct 2:14 occurrence after lexical review?

column2: Retain all remaining Ahab-house members in Jezreel, prominent men, acquaintances and priests, with no remnant left. The extended target groups are not collapsed into only royal sons; the pronoun his remains tied contextually to Ahab's house.

Retain rising and travel toward Samaria, with Baithakad of the shepherds on the road. The place remains in the selected position as the sentence leads into the encounter in verse 13; no confident sheep-shearing-house translation is substituted.

Retain Ahaziah's brothers, Jehu's identity question and their stated visit for the peace of the royal sons and the ruling lady's sons. Brothers is not silently changed to distant relatives, and ruling lady is not given an unexpressed personal name.
column3: Does for the peace denote a greeting/welfare visit, and how specifically should the ruling woman's status be expressed?

column2: Retain the order and execution of taking alive, followed by slaughter of forty-two at Baithakad and no survivor. The selected text does not specify a pit or cistern here; none is imported.

Retain Jonadab son of Rechab, meeting on the road, blessing, reciprocal heart-uprightness question, affirmative answer and exchanged hand before ascent into the chariot. Blessing may function as greeting, but the inherited term is retained rather than flattening the relational act.
Retain the invitation to see Jehu's zeal for the Lord Sabaoth and his seating of Jonadab in the chariot. The selected title is explicit and the final subject is singular, not an unnamed plural group.

Retain Samaria, all remaining of Ahab and the singular making him disappear according to the Lord's word to Elijah. Him is a house/dynasty reference in context, not a newly narrated death of the already dead Ahab.
column3: Would extinguished his house better express the corporate referent, or would it overdefine the selected singular object?

column2: Retain Jehu's claim that Ahab served Baal little and he will serve much. The deception is explained by the narrator in the next verse; no advance editorial adverb is inserted into this speech.

Retain the address to all Baal's prophets, summons for slaves and priests, threat against absence and great sacrifice. Trickery is explicitly narrated with the purpose of destroying Baal's slaves; it is not a conjectured motive.
Retain consecrating a sacrificial festival for Baal and its proclamation. Sacrificial festival is provisional for the selected hiereia; no detailed liturgy or duration is supplied.
column3: What is the precise cultic sense of hiereia here, and is sacrificial festival the best English expression?

column2: Retain the full repeated summons and threat, all three groups' arrival, no absentee and the house filled from mouth to mouth. The extended selected repetition is not removed, and the mouth image is not confidently reinterpreted as a measured architectural capacity.

Retain the one over the house of Mesthaal and the dresser bringing garments to every Baal slave. Mesthaal remains an unresolved house/office expression; it is not presented as an independently identified person's name.
column3: Does mesthaal denote a wardrobe, robe store or another administrative term, and how should it relate to the explicit dresser?

column2: Retain Jehu and Jonadab entering and the search for any Lord's slaves among exclusively Baal's slaves. Must supplies the directive force of the elliptical exclusivity clause; only/alone is supported by the selected restrictive wording.

Retain entering to perform sacrifices and whole burnt offerings, eighty men stationed outside and the life-for-life penalty. Both his-life phrases remain unresolved rather than silently being changed to your life for his life.
column3: Which life belongs to the escaping captive and which to the responsible guard; can explicit role labels be justified from the selected pronouns?

column2: Retain completion of the whole burnt offering, orders to runners and officers, no escape, sword killing, throwing and movement to the city of Baal's house. Them out supplies an object and direction contextually for the bare throwing verb; city remains a difficult selected noun.
column3: What is the object/direction of threw, and does city of Baal's house refer to a citadel, enclosure or another architectural unit?

column2: Retain singular Baal pillar brought out and burned. The material is not named, and the pillar is not changed to plural merely to align with the following verse.
Retain plural Baal pillars pulled down, house demolished and conversion to latrines to this day. The singular/plural sequence remains unharmonized; this day is the narrator's vantage.
Retain Jehu making Baal disappear from Israel. The statement is the narrative's summary of the preceding action and remains alongside the next verse's qualification about other cult objects.
Retain Jeroboam son of Nebat, his causing Israel to sin, Jehu's continued following and female golden heifers in Bethel and Dan. Heifers follows damaleis and is not silently changed to male bulls.

Retain the Lord's approval of doing right in His eyes, all His heart's intention toward Ahab's house and descendants to the fourth generation on Israel's throne. Fourth generation supplies the natural dynastic scope of sons fourth; no additional unlimited reign is implied.

Retain Jehu's failure to walk carefully in the Lord God's law with his whole heart and continued Jeroboam sins. The negative assessment is not suppressed to align with the preceding specific approval.

Retain the Lord beginning to cut down within Israel and Hazael striking across its territory. The divine and human agencies are both stated; the sentence continues into the east-Jordan geography rather than being generalized into an unspecified loss.
Retain eastward from Jordan, Gilead associated with Gad, Reuben and Manasseh, Aroer at Arnon's bank, and both Gilead and Bashan. The repeated Gilead is selected and is not deleted as duplication.
Retain Jehu's acts, all his power and the engagements he fought, followed by the annals question. The selected extra military clause remains; no Behold is inserted where this formula lacks it.
Retain laying down with fathers, burial in Samaria and Jehoahaz's succession. They buried is plural and the city remains explicit; no different tomb location is supplied.
Retain twenty-eight years of Jehu's reign in Samaria. The days/years idiom is naturally expressed without inventing a separate accession-year count.

Retain Athaliah as Ahaziah's mother, her seeing that plural sons had died and destruction of royal offspring. Sons is selected and is not reduced to one son to match the preceding king's death notice; the rescue exception follows in the narrative.

Retain Jehosheba's father and sibling relation, Joash as her brother's son, rescue from the killings, nurse, chamber of beds and concealment from Athaliah. The complex hiding-location syntax remains provisional; Joash's survival is explicit.
column3: Does the chamber-of-beds phrase describe where the pair were first placed or the act of hiding, and can the sentence be clarified without adding a missing placement verb?

column2: Retain Joash with her in the Lord's house, six years hidden and Athaliah reigning over the land. The two simultaneous situations remain, without a new claim about her knowledge of the hiding place.

Retain the seventh year, priest Jehoiada, captains of hundreds, Chorri and Rasim, covenant of the Lord, oath before Him and showing the king's son. The guard names remain unresolved rather than automatically equated with ethnic units.
column3: How should Chorri and Rasim be understood as names or guard designations, and how do they relate to the captains syntactically?

column2: Retain the command, first third entering on Sabbath and guarding the king's house at the gateway. The sentence continues into the other two thirds; no complete guard-shift schedule is reconstructed beyond the stated arrangement.
Retain the Gate of the Roads, gate behind the runners and house watch. The selected gate name is not substituted with Sur; which house is meant in the final clause remains contextual.

Retain two divisions, all going out on Sabbath and guarding the Lord's house for the king. Divisions interprets hands as troop groups, but the relation to the preceding three thirds is not mathematically reconstructed as settled fact.

Retain the king's encirclement, each man's equipment, death for entry into saderoth and the selected third-person he was with the king. The final clause is not silently changed to an imperative be with the king; the subject and guard term remain open.
column3: What does saderoth denote, and who is the subject of the unexpected third-person narrative clause after the commands?

column2: Retain captains carrying out all instructions, Jehoiada the discerning one, each man's incoming and outgoing Sabbath groups, and arrival at Jehoiada the priest. The unusual discerning epithet is not erased or made into a second person.

Retain David's lances and threefold weapons from the Lord's house. Threefold weapons is a provisional attempt at the substantival trissous, not an approved identification as shields or a particular weapon design.
column3: What military object is denoted by trissous here, and can a defensible English noun replace the provisional threefold weapons?

column2: Retain runners each armed, right-to-left house flanks, altar/house relation and encirclement of the king. Beside supplies a spatial connection for the compressed Greek layout; a precise architectural plan remains unverified.
column3: How do the altar and house genitives relate to the right/left flanks and the surrounding formation?

column2: Retain the king's son brought out, nezer and testimony placed on him, singular making king/anointing and plural hand-clapping/acclamation. Nezer remains unresolved as an object term; testimony is not silently replaced by an identified scroll.
column3: What objects are nezer and testimony in this coronation, and does placing them upon him imply wearing or presentation?

column2: Retain Athaliah hearing the running people's sound and entering among them in the Lord's house. The selected phrase is not automatically separated into guards and people as two independently named groups.

Propose and behold, the king was standing for and there was the king standing to retain the presentative. Pillar, ordinance, singers and trumpets, rejoicing people, torn garments and doubled Conspiracy remain; singers are not replaced with commanders.

Retain priest Jehoiada's order through captains/overseers, removal from inside saderoth, death by sword for a follower and the reason she must not die in the Lord's house. Inside is selected and is not silently reversed into outside the ranks.
column3: How should inside the saderoth be understood spatially, especially in the command to bring her out?

column2: Retain hands laid on Athaliah, her movement by the horses' entrance to the king's house and death there. The selected active she entered leaves escort agency implicit; the later verse specifies sword death, but no extra method is added here.

Retain covenant relations among Lord, king and people for being the Lord's people, followed by the king/people relation. The repetition is not collapsed, and no unexpressed terms of the covenant are supplied.

Retain all the land's people demolishing Baal's house, thoroughly breaking altars/images, killing Mattan before the altars and the priest's appointment of overseers for the Lord's house. The collective actors and final singular priest remain distinct.

Retain captains, Chorri, Rasim and all the people, descent from the Lord's house, entry by the Runners' Gate and seating on the kings' throne. The single entering subject is naturally the king, while those seating him are plural; no guard group is dropped.

Retain the people's rejoicing, quiet city and Athaliah's sword death in the king's house. Had put presents the final death statement as a recap of verse 16; the selected chapter ends here, with Joash's age reserved for the next chapter.
